skill.name: cm
skill.description: CM provides procedural memory for AI coding agents by turning session history into reusable playbook rules, feedback, and task context.
skill.summary: Share durable coding memory across Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and other agents.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and command examples. Real risks remain around remote installer execution, public MCP serving, privileged installation, and privacy-sensitive session history access. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Remote install script is piped directly to bash.
remediation.suggestion: Publish signed releases or checksums and instruct users to inspect downloaded scripts before execution.

remediation.issue: MCP server documentation includes a 0.0.0.0 binding example.
remediation.suggestion: Keep loopback as the default and document strong tokens, TLS, firewall rules, and least-privilege network access.

remediation.issue: The tool consumes and stores agent session history.
remediation.suggestion: Document consent, retention, redaction, and export controls before indexing Claude, Codex, or remote sessions.

remediation.issue: Source install instructions use sudo to move a binary into /usr/local/bin.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer user-local installation paths and require users to verify build output before privileged installation.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Install Script Piped To Shell
semantic_findings.description: The installation workflow recommends fetching install.sh from GitHub raw content and piping it to bash. This can execute changed remote code before the user reviews a pinned artifact.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 798-799 directly combine a remote curl download with shell execution, which is a known supply-chain risk.

semantic_findings.title: Network-Exposed MCP Memory Server
semantic_findings.description: The non-loopback MCP example binds the server to all interfaces and exposes memory tools. A weak token or network misconfiguration could expose session-derived context.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command uses --host 0.0.0.0 and the adjacent table lists context, feedback, outcome, search, and reflection tools.

semantic_findings.title: Privacy-Sensitive Cross-Agent Session Ingestion
semantic_findings.description: The skill turns raw session logs from multiple agents into shared memory and shows hidden Claude and Codex session paths. Those logs may contain private prompts, source code, and secrets.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly describes raw agent sessions as memory input and shows hidden session file paths in the output model.

content.user_title: Build Shared Memory for AI Coding Agents
content.value_statement: AI coding agents lose useful decisions when sessions end. CM turns session history into reusable rules, feedback, and task context across Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Retrieves task-specific rules, anti-patterns, history snippets, and suggested CASS searches.
Manages playbook rules with add, remove, import, export, feedback, and provenance commands.
Reflects session history into reusable guidance through generator, validator, and curator stages.
Exposes MCP tools for context retrieval, feedback, outcomes, memory search, and reflection.
Documents privacy controls, local data paths, budget limits, and JSON output modes.
Provides trauma guard commands and hooks for dangerous command patterns.
limitations: Requires the external CM and CASS command line tools to be installed.
Some reflection and validation workflows may need provider API keys.
Uses local session history, so users must manage consent and redaction carefully.
Installation examples include remote scripts and privileged commands that need review.

best_practices: Run context retrieval before substantial coding tasks, then reference rule IDs during the work.
Keep cross-agent enrichment opt-in and review privacy settings before indexing sessions.
Prefer local-only MCP serving unless network access is required and secured.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installers into a shell without independent verification.
Do not expose the MCP server on all interfaces with weak or shared tokens.
Do not import private session logs into shared playbooks without consent.

faq.question: What does CM store?
faq.answer: It stores playbook rules, diary entries, outcomes, trauma patterns, and related local memory files.

faq.question: Does CM require cloud sync?
faq.answer: The documentation describes a local-first design with no cloud sync or telemetry.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill targets shared context across Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and other coding agents.

faq.question: When are API keys needed?
faq.answer: Some LLM-based reflection and validation workflows may require Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google API keys.

faq.question: What is trauma guard?
faq.answer: It records dangerous command patterns and can install hooks to block repeated unsafe actions.

faq.question: What should users review before install?
faq.answer: Users should review remote installer commands, sudo usage, MCP binding, and session privacy settings.
